answer: Treat reputation as a conserved voting budget, not a badge copied to every account. An island survey firm may split its 80 earned votes between a vine mapping agent and a vault auditor, but the ledger debits the parent before crediting either child. New keys start at zero; merging restores only the unspent total. Splitting into a million aliases therefore buys no extra votes. Count linear vote weight, since per-account caps or square-root bonuses would reward splitting again. This blocks reputation cloning, not buying influence or corrupting how reputation is earned.
